title: On Negotiating the price for two whole days
subtitle: 经济消费 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）
meta: 主题语境：经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）　|　核心词汇：negotiate　|　正文 347 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 negotiate 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 the craftsman ① negotiated the price for two whole days before dawn, and every apprentice in the workshop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the craftsman ② negotiates the price for two whole days in public without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ negotiate the price for two whole days at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ negotiated the price for two whole days before — a line in the ledger for August 1942 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Negotiating the price for two whole days before dawn, the craftsman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the tool at the far bench, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ negotiate the bend without mishap in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Negotiate the bend without mishap at once and never mention it again.

By 1955 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the ledger, and a new apprentice from the next workshop ⑧ negotiates the bend without mishap before dawn every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the bench, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ negotiated the price for two whole days again when nobody else would.

⑩ To negotiate the price for two whole days, my mother said in 1960, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the workshop remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the workshop forgets, somebody negotiates the price for two whole days in public again and somebody must negotiate the price for two whole days before dawn all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 谈判（一般过去式 negotiated the price for two whole days：1948 年匠人头一回这样做，天没亮就）
B. v. 谈判（一般现在 negotiates the price for two whole days：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 谈判（不定式 to negotiate the price for two whole days：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 谈判（过去完成时 had negotiated the price for two whole days：1942 年八月的工料簿上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 谈判（动名词 negotiating the price for two whole days 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 顺利通过（negotiate the bend without mishap：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去顺利通过平安无事地驶过那道弯）
G. v. 顺利通过（negotiate the bend without mishap：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 谈判（后段两处：新来的学徒照例 negotiates the bend without mishap，而母亲又一次 negotiated the price for two whole days）

answers.why: negotiate 意为“谈判”，1948 年匠人天没亮就谈判为价钱谈了整整两天，那是工坊里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 negotiated。
negotiate 意为“谈判”，自那以后匠人当着众人面把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 negotiates。
negotiate 意为“谈判”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯谈判为价钱谈了整整两天”，此处为不定式 to negotiate the price for two whole days。
negotiate 意为“谈判”，工料簿里 八月 那行字说明早在 1955 年之前就有人谈判过，故用过去完成时 had negotiated。
negotiate 意为“谈判”，匠人说“谈判为价钱谈了整整两天这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 negotiating the price for two whole days 作主语。
negotiate 意为“顺利通过”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去顺利通过平安无事地驶过那道弯”，should ever 之后用原形 negotiate the bend without mishap。
negotiate 意为“顺利通过”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻顺利通过平安无事地驶过那道弯（negotiate the bend without mishap at once），以后再也不要提起。
negotiate 意为“谈判”，新来的学徒每个年头都照例顺利通过平安无事地驶过那道弯，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 negotiates。
negotiate 意为“谈判”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次天没亮就谈判为价钱谈了整整两天，用一般过去式 negotiated 叙述。
negotiate 意为“谈判”，结尾那句是母亲 1960 年的话：要谈判为价钱谈了整整两天，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和工坊记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 negotiate 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1948 the craftsman negotiated the price for two whole days before dawn, and nobody in the workshop forgot it.
Even now the craftsman negotiates the price for two whole days in public whenever the workshop asks.
Negotiating the price for two whole days before dawn, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever negotiate the bend without mishap in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new apprentice from the next workshop negotiates the bend without mishap before dawn every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother negotiated the price for two whole days again, and the workshop remembered that half.
